subject: Post-call: Hightide Retail discovery + tech recap
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>

Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-call: Hightide Retail discovery + tech recap

Hi Elena / Tom — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re all aligned and to capture next steps.

Summary of key pain points
- High tail latency on personalized recommendations during peak shopping windows (~18:00–23:00 PST).
- Current infra struggles to keep up with bursts around promotions (Black Friday–like spikes but on a weekly cadence).
- Cost unpredictability from existing model serving; infra spend spikes when traffic surges.

Goals you shared
- 99th percentile latency target: <= 120ms per request for the recommender endpoint (inference only).
- Sustained throughput target: 2,500 QPS during peak windows, with ability to burst to 4,000 QPS for short periods.
- Multi-region redundancy (US West + US East) with failover.
- Data residency: logs and telemetry stored in customer VPC; no raw PII leaves environment.

Model/tech notes from call
- Model family: transformer-based recommender (decoder-only hybrid; ~7B parameters after pruning).
- Cacheable prefix usage: heavy reuse of user-prefix embeddings across sessions — good candidate for prefix/KV caching.
- Some experiments use quantized weights (4-bit). You indicated a willingness to trade small accuracy delta for cost.

Initial recommendations (quick):
- Private Dedicated deployment into your VPC with isolated GPU pools for the recommender route.
- Enable KV prefix caching and throughput-aware batching policy for the endpoint.
- Canary rollout for model changes with automatic fallback to a smaller variant during degradation.

Attachments: I’ve included an XLSX you mentioned for QPS estimates and the network diagram you promised (see attachments section).

Next steps / action items
- Hightide: share expected 95/99 latency distribution from your prod telemetry and any SLO/alert thresholds (Tom).
- Hightide: confirm compliance requirements for logs retention and KMS (Elena).
- Redwood: run a feasibility pre-read and draft a proposed topology + cost ballpark (Neha).
- Schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive with SRE + infra owners next week — suggested times Thursday/Friday morning PST.

I’ll loop in Neha (Solutions Eng) who’ll propose a technical plan and a short benchmark plan we can run against a small lift-and-shift sample.

Thanks,
Rafael
Sales Lead, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Post-call: Hightide Retail discovery + tech recap — technical addendum

Hi team — following Rafa’s recap, I put together a short technical note with concrete options based on the targets you mentioned. High level first, then specifics.

High-level recommendation (pref):
- Private Dedicated (Redwood Dedicated) in your AWS account (us-west-2) using a VPC peering model. Benefits: full telemetry/logging into your account + KMS/HSM control, predictable throughput via dedicated GPU pools.
- Multi-AZ in us-west-2 for immediate redundancy; cross-region warm standby in us-east-1 for failover.

Deployment topology (details):
- Inference tier: 2x GPU nodes in active-active per AZ for baseline capacity (NVidia A100-class equivalent) sized to sustain 2,500 QPS with batching and prefix caching.
- Burst capacity: autoscale to additional dedicated nodes; fast path uses pre-warmed pool for 4k QPS short bursts.
- Cache: KV prefix cache co-located with serving nodes (in-memory) to reduce decoder steps for repeated user prefixes.
- Routing: smart routing policy for regional failover and model-variant fallback (e.g., quantized 4-bit variant if latency deteriorates).

Latency & batching guidance:
- Target inference-only P99 <= 80–100ms with batching disabled for tail-sensitive traffic; use small, time-limited batching windows (1–4ms) for throughput-sensitive flows.
- Continuous batching should be workload-aware: prioritize requests that benefit from batching (non-real-time recommendations) and route low-latency traffic through reserved low-concurrency replicas.

Model sizing & quantization:
- For the ~7B hybrid model, we expect ~32GB GPU memory for FP16; 4-bit quantization reduces memory footprint significantly and supports higher packing/batching.
- Suggest an A/B of FP16 vs 4-bit quantized 1% sampling in canary to measure accuracy delta before full rollout.

Benchmarks & tests we propose to run (small scope):
- Synthetic QPS ramp test to 4k sustained for 5 minutes to validate autoscale and warm-pool latency.
- Prefix-cache hit-rate evaluation using a week of anonymized traffic sample.
- Failure injection (AZ outage) to validate failover latency and route convergence.

Preliminary cost notes (ballpark):
- Baseline monthly committed capacity (2 dedicated GPU nodes per AZ) + burst credits. We’ll provide a cost matrix once we validate exact instance SKUs.

Attachments: redwood-config-proposal.pdf (topology diagram + config parameters), benchmark-matrix.csv (example test matrix).

If the Thursday deep-dive works, I’ll prepare a short runbook and we can invite your SRE and platform engineers to walk through telemetry/KMS details.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
